blind.B1: Yes. In vivo human resistance-exercise study (10 trained females, cross-over NS vs SR, REx on days 3,5,7,9; S2.2.p2). Only PRE-exercise vastus lateralis biopsies on day 3 and day 9 were sequenced (S2.7.p1), so the exercise factor is the training effect (day 9 vs day 3, 48 h after the last session), not an acute response; the SR vs NS contrasts carry no acute exercise (S3.2.p2). No non-exercise arm.
blind.B2: NS day 9 vs NS day 3 (paper 2962 DEGs: 128 up / 2834 down, S3.2.p7); SR day 9 vs SR day 3 (2219: 102 up / 2117 down); SR vs NS day 3 (1 DEG, GGNBP2); SR vs NS day 9 (0 DEG) (S3.2.p2, S3.2.p7). 10 participants x 2 conditions x 2 days = 40 planned; GEO has 38 (NS_D3 9, SR_D3 10, NS_D9 10, SR_D9 9; SASY has two samples).
blind.B3: Yes. Cross-over: every participant is sampled in both conditions and on both days (up to 4 biopsies each). Candidate key: the 4-letter prefix of the sample title / the metadata `subject` column (10 keys, 38/38 samples linked, no duplicates within a group level).
blind.B4: S2.8.p1: 'Differential expression analysis was performed using all RNA sequencing samples to compare NS and SR conditions by day, as well as the same condition by day' with DESeq (v1.40.2); the design formula is not stated, so one joint model is implied but participant blocking is not documented. The linear mixed models with participant random intercepts (S2.12.p1) are for protein/gene-expression outcomes, not for the DESeq analysis.
blind.B5: S2.8.p1: 'significance thresholds set with an adjusted p-value of < 0.05 and Log2 fold change > 1 and <-1'; figure legends FIG1/FIG3 repeat |log2FC| > 1 and p-adjusted < 0.05. Results counts are labelled 'FDR < 0.05' only (S3.2.p7, S3.3.p2). Reported counts: 1 and 0 for SR vs NS; 2962 (128/2834) and 2219 (102/2117) for D9 vs D3.

checks.evidence: Run as a training/time contrast (day 9 pre vs day 3 pre), explicitly not an acute response (study caveats, HANDBACK); matches B1.

packet B level table: cond NS 19 / SR 19, day D3 19 / D9 19, cells 9/10/10/9 as in GEO metadata; no exclusions; the missing SASY samples are recorded in paper_data_discrepancies.json. Controls are the same-condition day 3 (exercise) and NS (sleep), as in the paper.

Contrasts are treatment=D9 over control=D3 and SR over NS (design gate), i.e. exercise over control. The paper's text direction differs (oxidative metabolism 'up', GGNBP2 'up' in SR) but its panel labels NS3_vs_NS9 / NS3_vs_SR3 are reference-over-test; our GGNBP2 log2FC(SR/NS) = -2.27 and OXPHOS NES -2.57 are consistent with that reading. Recorded in study caveats and HANDBACK.
Participant (title prefix, 10 levels, categorical) is a blocking term in the primary fit ~ subject + cell; design check full rank, residual df 26; unblocked fit kept as sensitivity.
One joint model on all 38 samples follows S2.8.p1. Paper formula silent and counts differ a lot (blocked FDR-only 4003/2943 vs unblocked 2965/2224 vs paper 2962/2219), and both fits are reported.

Training effect is confounded with time in condition and is labelled so. Cross-over order / washout length (SR first with 12-week washout, S2.2.p1) and the unequal NS/SR living conditions are not recorded as possible aliases of cond; no sequencing batch is deposited.
checks.fix: Optional: add one caveat line on condition order and in-lab vs home setting.

checks.evidence: Integer fraction 1.0, rounded Kallisto gene counts, DESeq2 route; mean>=10 filter reproduces the paper's 15,543 genes; frac_p_gt_0.9 0.05 and frac_p_lt_0.05 0.32-0.37 for exercise contrasts, no p-value pile-up.

Applied rule transcribes S2.8.p1 exactly (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1, strict). The paper's counts fit unblocked padj < 0.05 only (2965 vs 2962; 2224 vs 2219), and this is recorded in the audit threshold, study caveats and paper_data_discrepancies.json. The mechanical flag's 'closest rule' (pvalue<0.05 & |lfc|>0.585) is not the best fit; the recorded one is better.

Same four contrasts compared; HANDBACK shows all rules side by side. Its statement that the paper 'did not block on participant' is an inference from count agreement, not from the paper text, and the paper's up/down split is explained as non-sign-based.

human_items: Open policy question: which threshold to report as headline when the paper's counts fit FDR-only unblocked (2965/2224) but its Methods state FDR + |log2FC| > 1; the case applies the stated rule and reports the other as audit.

Paper's stated directions (oxidative metabolism up with training, GGNBP2 up with SR) are opposite to the data under exercise-over-control ordering; the analysis attributes this to reference-over-test labels (NS3_vs_NS9). A person may want to confirm with the authors before any direction-dependent claim is quoted against the paper.
Primary fit blocks on participant while the paper's counts match the unblocked fit; joint blocked vs unblocked as the primary is an open policy choice when the paper is silent.
summary: 该案例通过审查：运行决定、分组（38个样本，4个单元9/10/10/9）、对比方向（运动对照）、以受试者为区块的配对模型、阈值转录均与论文一致，并已记录例外。论文的DEG数量与未分区块、仅FDR<0.05的拟合吻合，已作为审计与敏感性分析如实报告。论文文字中的方向与数据相反，分析已解释为对比标签写成参考对检验，建议人工确认。
